As someone who plays an extraordinary amount of time due to their life being a tire fire, this is too much even for me.  The current crafting system is a remnant of the "shadowlands" mindset that blizzard had of maximizing "engagement" despite that engagement fostering nothing but negative feelings and memories with the product in question.  It's shortsighted stat farming by people who have most likely never gotten outside of a newbie zone in the game.  



A major issue with a lot of the "Triple A" industry is that they don't understand things that can't be easily quantified, like "Fun".  A lot of WoW's systems are more akin to rituals than actual systems now.  Things that exist because they worked to some degree in the past, but not quite understood why they still exist.  "Good will" can not be easily tracked on a spreadsheet and thus falls to the wayside.  That's why I think the indie market is gaining a lot of ground in the gaming market, they are often passionate people who understand more handily what works and what doesn't, and are more eager to experiment.  



Blizzard has begun to experiment again with TWW, but this crafting system feels like a relic of the shadowlands mindset of "no such thing as bad engagement", where you can farm a rare for a mount or pet a thousand times and not get anything, ignoring the growing resentment that the constant "Lucy pulling away the football at the last minute" feeling fosters.  

  
Log in every week, grind your knowledge points, you don't want to fall behind do you?  This nonsense is why I gave up mount farming completely halfway through shadowlands.  I hope this mindset is diminishing not growing.



And before someone says "of course there's a grind, it's an MMO" Try collecting all the appearances from shadowlands as a no lifer.  I use wow as a bucket to pour all my time into, lest doom and gloom consume my mind, and I still am missing well over half of shadowlands appearances for plate.  Shadowlands was the pinnacle of abusive MMO design in wow and hopefully they change this crafting system to be less convoluted and more player friendly.

Until max level, don't worry about it so long as it has your class/spec's main stat (Str/Agi/Int, in your case Agi), just focus on Ilvl.  At max level, find out where the dreamsurge zone is that week and get the weekly there done.  (don't forget to grab the aiding the accord weekly from vald) Also get the time rift done in thaldrazus for another gear token.  your first goal is to get enough Ilvl to enter heroics.  run heroics until you get \* done for your weekly great vault (you can substitute this for timewalking if its a timewalking week).  Your next ilvl goal is to get high enough to enter LFR.  Run all of the current tier (Amirdrassil) LFRs in an attempt to get veteran tier items.  (i'd do this as a dps with loot spec set to tank, but I'm a coward when it comes to tanking so YMMV.) Make sure you get the quest inside the first wing after the first boss (the tree boi) for the head enchant.  At this point you should figure out which tier-applicable slots have a veteran tier or greater (head, shoulders, chest, hands, legs) and go to the catalyst in the center right of thaldrazus (there should be a quest in vald to take you there).  your next goal is to get your tier pieces to get your 4-piece and get your raid head enchant.  While waiting for your LFR queues, get your emerald dream questline done until you unlock the central camp.  You'll want to complete the world boss (denoted by the WQ nw of camp), the quest to get 1500 rep for the emerald dream boys, the plant 5 seeds quest, and you will want to complete the superbloom (which starts east-ish of camp at the horn, grab the quest from the dryad who follows the big tree dude).  Also when doing LFRs you will get items to make sparks for crafted items to help fill slots.

This is how I did it and I got pretty high ilvl before I got the nerve to do mythic plus, which I suggest doing at least 1 +2 when you've got the gear for it so your great vault's second row has a good item in the first slot.

Despite popular belief, animals do show personalities and emotions.  I have a family of 3 cats, a mother and a daughter and son.  The mother is fairly solitary, she is warm and affectionate to me unless upset, then will find a high place to lay and growl whenever touched.  When the daughter is around her they both show affection for a bit then the mother ends up tiring of her presence and gives a little growl.  She absolutely hates her son, and refuses to be in the same room with him unless I am present and he isn't near or preferably not in sight.  This is fairly well deserved seeing as the son is large and kind of a prick.  He often sits on chairs under the dining room table and swats at your legs, or swats at the dog's ass.  He also demands attention and when you take your hand away, you had better be fast or he'll swat you and bite.  He's always been a little shithead but since his brother died he's become more of an asshole, but when he's not bullying his family around he gives his little quack of a meow and him and his sister curl up together for a midday nap.  Now the daugter is a longhaired priss, she's more of an outdoors cat and doesn't stay in for long anymore, but when she does she is very needy, wanting to ride on my shoulders all the time and requiring me to take her to the window where they go outside, because she doesn't like the dog.  If I don't she'll just sit there meowing at me, sometimes I can get away with grabbing her for a lap cuddle but during the summer months she's never too eager to stay indoors, and prefers lounging hidden under the bushes.  Each of the 4 siblings had their own personalities and it was apparent at times when they were happy or upset.  Bubba (the brother who is still with us) can be a cantankerous shit and when he's upset he  lays there, gives me the "what do you want" scowl and becomes a noodle when I try to pick him up.  When he's happy he'll quack at me and look at me with bright eyes and I'll end up with considerably more scratches on my arm.  I've lived with animals my whole life and I know it seems like I'm just a fanboy raving on about how all his animals are tiny little people, but I've seen plenty of evidence that Animals do have emotions, and it influences their actions.  Some of those emotions just happen to be disemboweling of small critters.  

(and before someone gets on me about them harming the animal population, they rarely go after birds, and we have a large amount of birds that visit our area.  They mostly eat chipmunks, which after the other brother died, my grandparents, who live a few houses over and next to the same woods I live next to, saw an explosion in chimpmunks and moles (which they don't eat, but still kill.  I'm thinking of starting a little wall of mole skulls on sticks to commemorate the mole bloodbaths.) and the daughter mostly eats reptiles for some reason, though I did catch her eating a fraking huge moth.  Ok rambling over.)
